verdicts.why: The note's actual claim about the word is that it approves nothing, explicitly assigning the cool/warm contrast to the referents rather than the words, which fits the neutral label and the gloss.
Places the compound among its -scented neighbours and says it states its source without verdict, which fits 'smelling of musk' and the neutral label.
Thin but inside the word: same sense as musk-scented, a remark on form, no verdict claimed, matching the neutral label.
Maps the gloss's three prongs (having, covered with, accompanied by) and calls the word non-judging, which fits the neutral base; all four examples fit this literal sense.
Describes 'containing blood' as a fact of contents with no verdict, contrasted with the open base; neutral label and example fit.
Stays on 'covered with blood' and locates the word's force in the stain that mars, which makes the negative label plausible; example fits.
Same covering as bloodstained turned lurid and spectacular with recoil built in; negative fits the gloss and 'a gory dagger' fits the sense.

Keeps to the literal drawing of blood from another's body and explains the word's recoil as the feeding-off frame rather than violence, without sliding into the separate figurative parasite sense; example fits.
Reads the 'eagerness' of the gloss as appetite and condemns the wanting; negative fits and 'bloodthirsty yells' fits this sense.
Sites the same eagerness in temperament, distinguishing it from bloodthirsty without importing the British obstinate sense; negative and example fit.
Formal is a permitted register label, and the arm's-length condemnation of an eagerness for bloodshed stays on the gloss; example fits.
Describes the figure of naming violence by colour so the judgement arrives as image, which is what the word does under this gloss; both examples fit.
Same figure as crimson with less heightening, on the violence/bloodshed gloss; 'convulsed with red rage' fits this sense.
Says the word states outright what its figurative neighbours imply, and its reach across 'violence or bloodshed' matches the gloss's disjunction.
Clinical is a register label, and the note maps the gloss's three prongs (tendency, capacity, character of the act); negative and example fit.
Same range as homicidal with the weight of the crime added, condemning as it describes; negative fits and 'murderous thugs' fits.
Formal and cool are register facts; 'bloodshed attends' is the gloss, and a word that marks bloodshed as attending is plausibly negative even while contrasted with sanguinary's appetite.
Describes the word's force (wholesale, scale) rather than narrowing what it refers to, staying on 'accompanied by bloodshed'; negative fits.
